column5: What if every spider on Earth hunted together?
There are over fifty thousand kinds of spiders.
Together they weigh about twenty-five million tons.
And every year, they eat up to eight hundred million tons of prey.
That's up to twice what all humans eat in meat and fish.
If they ever worked as one… no forest, field or house would be safe.
In the tropics of the Americas, thousands share one giant web… and take down prey far bigger than themselves.
Without spiders, the world would be crawling with insects.
Would you let one live in your house?
